---
title: "Knowledge Distillation"
description: "Training a smaller student model to imitate a larger teacher model's behavior."
term: "Knowledge Distillation"
letter: "K"
category: "Model Optimization"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large, often expensive model
into a smaller or faster model. The student learns to reproduce the teacher's
outputs or soft probabilities, rather than starting from scratch.

## Technical explanation

A teacher model is trained on a task and then used to generate outputs, often
soft probabilities, for examples in a dataset. The student model is trained
with a loss that combines the task loss and a distillation loss that encourages
it to match the teacher's soft targets. This can improve compact models by
exposing them to richer supervision than hard labels alone.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Distillation is useful when deploying models under memory, latency, or
cost constraints. It enables a smaller model to capture much of the teacher's
performance while reducing inference expense and resource use.

## How it works

The teacher produces soft targets, often by taking a temperature-scaled
softmax over logits. The student is trained to match those targets and the true
labels. This encourages the student to learn information about relative class
confidence that may be lost when only one label is used for supervision.

## Practical example

A large language model can serve as a teacher for a smaller student model that
must run on a mobile device. The student is trained to match the teacher's
responses or distribution over next-token options, while still being efficient
enough for deployment.

## Common misconceptions

- Distillation is not just a smaller copy of the teacher; the student still needs appropriate training and evaluation.
- Soft targets are helpful, but they do not guarantee the student will generalize well.
- A compact student may still fail if the data or task is poorly matched to the teacher's strengths.
